claim: Provenance recovery must optimize a precision-recall tradeoff; recovering more true dependencies can worsen truth estimates if independent sources are falsely merged.
scope: Experiment 002A generated source families and registered recovery algorithms.
support: Hybrid recall was 0.8671 versus citation recall 0.4040.
Hybrid precision was 0.6123 versus citation precision 1.0000.
Overall hybrid Brier was 0.08770 versus citation Brier 0.07977.

confidence.rationale: The favored hybrid method failed preregistered H5 and H6 despite superior recall; the result is deterministic within the registered grid.

boundary: The relative costs depend on the generator, clustering rule, and downstream loss; other hybrid methods may control false merging.
disconfirmation: A preregistered replication under the same generator shows that hybrid's recall gain improves downstream loss without adequate precision.
Real-corpus studies show no meaningful downstream cost from false source-family mergers.
action_implication: Evaluate provenance systems on downstream probabilistic loss and both error directions, not F1 or recall alone.

claim: In the registered benchmark, false mergers of independent evidence families were more damaging than false splits of dependent reports.
scope: Experiment 002A binary truth synthesis, in which a false merger removes an independent likelihood contribution and a false split repeats a correlated one.
support: Citation-only recovery had zero false-dependence rate, 59.6% false-independence rate, and Brier 0.07977.
Hybrid recovery had 30.7% false-dependence rate, 13.3% false-independence rate, and Brier 0.08770.
Hybrid precision below the preregistered 0.90 requirement caused H5 to fail.

confidence.rationale: The direction is clear across the registered aggregate, but its magnitude and transfer depend on the decision loss.

boundary: This is not a universal asymmetry. In other applications, repeated correlated evidence may be more damaging than suppressing an independent source.
disconfirmation: Decision-specific replications with the same asymmetry show false splits create greater expected loss.
The result disappears under realistic source reliability and multi-parent modeling.
action_implication: High-consequence provenance tools should default to precision-first grouping or uncertainty bounds until false-merge costs are estimated.

claim: Unconditional union of citation and similarity edges can amplify error through transitive closure even when it guarantees higher recall.
scope: Connected-component clustering over the union of registered citation and Jaccard-similarity edges.
support: Hybrid recall exceeded both component methods, but hybrid precision was only 61.2%.
A false similarity bridge could merge two citation components, causing every cross-component pair to become a predicted dependency.
Preregistered H5 failed despite hybrid's recall advantage.

confidence.rationale: The amplification mechanism follows directly from connected-component closure and appears in the registered results.

invariance: Structural property of unconditional transitive closure.
boundary: Probabilistic clustering, bridge-edge validation, temporal constraints, or non-transitive relationship types may prevent the failure.
disconfirmation: A formal error shows that false bridge edges cannot induce component-wide mergers.
A constrained hybrid method eliminates the mechanism while preserving recall.
action_implication: Audit bridge edges and avoid treating all provenance relations as automatically transitive equivalence relations.

claim: Hybrid provenance recovery may be highly useful when topical collision is low and harmful when collision is high.
scope: Post-run exploratory contamination stratification in Experiment 002A.
support: At contamination 0.10, hybrid precision was 1.0000, recall 0.8027, and Brier 0.0685 versus 0.0866 for all-independent synthesis.
At contamination 0.50, hybrid precision was 0.2245, false-dependence rate 0.6142, and Brier 0.1069 versus 0.0886 for all-independent synthesis.

confidence.rationale: The contrast is large and mechanistically coherent but was identified through post-run stratification rather than a frozen confirmatory contrast.

invariance: Observed across registered root counts, family sizes, citation levels, and paraphrase rates within each contamination stratum.
boundary: Topic contamination is a simplified generator parameter, not a directly measured real-world quantity.
disconfirmation: A preregistered replication fails to reproduce the interaction.
Natural-language benchmarks show similarity precision is unrelated to topical collision.
action_implication: The next method should estimate collision risk and abstain or widen uncertainty when unrelated sources share dense vocabulary.

claim: Whether real evidence ancestry can be recovered with adequate precision remains unknown.
scope: Transfer from generated token documents to natural scholarly, journalistic, historical, intelligence, and agent-produced artifacts.
support: Experiment 002A used disjoint known families, missing but never false citations, and auditable token transformations.
Two central hybrid-method hypotheses failed, demonstrating that structural inference can backfire even in the simplified setting.

confidence.rationale: The limitation is entailed by the study design.

boundary: This does not claim real recovery is impossible; it identifies the next empirical question.
disconfirmation: Experiment 002B demonstrates calibrated, generalizable recovery on adjudicated real corpora with downstream gains.
action_implication: Do not deploy inferred point dependence weights in high-consequence inquiries before real-corpus validation; use ranges and audit trails.
